title: Model Supply Compass: Scouting-to-Provision Playbook
creator: Aisha Navarro
description:
Purpose: create a lightweight, repeatable playbook and scoring heuristic that lets PM/Field/Platform quickly scout emerging open models and translate signals into a provisioning recommendation (hosted / dedicated / private) and a measured integration effort estimate.

Why: model churn and proliferation continues to accelerate. Sales and SRE teams need fast, defensible decisions when customers request new model variants or when a popular open model surfaces. Ad-hoc decisions are causing inconsistent SLAs, unplanned infra spend, and slow time-to-resolution.

Scope: signal ingestion (benchmarks, license, quant readiness, hardware fit, community traction), heuristic scoring, minimal evaluation checklist, gating criteria for onboarding into our catalog, handoff templates for ENG/Research, and alerting thresholds for procurement or dev resources.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A documented scoring heuristic (latency/cost/quality/risk) with weights and rationale; 2) A 5-step scout checklist that can be executed in 1-2 engineer-hours; 3) An initial rule-set mapping score ranges to provisioning recommendation (hosted/dedicated/private) and estimated integration points; 4) A Playbook doc in Confluence and a short internal launch email; 5) Two pilot scouts executed and recorded with retrospective notes.
deliverables: Confluence: Model Supply Compass playbook v1
Scoring spreadsheet template and scripted starter metrics
tradeoffs: Favor speed of qualification over exhaustive evaluation in v1 — early false negatives (declaring a model unready) will be handled by an explicit appeal process. We accept some variance in integration point estimates to make the process lightweight. Heuristic weights are configurable; we prioritize operational cost and license risk for enterprise provisioning recommendations.
